title: AssetInventory
description: Agent B's (Archive/Visual Editor) record of REAL discovered assets, plus coverage reporting against every producer_outline.json visual_request. This schema defines the data contract only -- searching/downloading is not implemented yet. Central rule: DISCOVERY IS NOT VERIFICATION. Finding a plausible search result is not the same as having looked at the thing.

status.description: pending: Agent B has not run. gathered: every visual_request has a request_coverage entry. approved: reviewed. Agent A's A4 stage is gated on this reaching gathered or approved -- see agents/agent_a_producer_writer.md.

environment_limitations.description: Capabilities this run genuinely lacked, stated plainly rather than hidden -- e.g. 'cannot decode video frames, so no video asset can exceed verification_method: metadata_only', or 'domain X blocks this crawler'. A limitation recorded here is the justification for weaker verification_method values elsewhere in the file.

matched_request_ids.description: producer_outline.json visual_request request_id values this asset addresses

source_url.description: Where the asset lives. At least one of source_url or local_path must be present -- an asset with neither is not a discovered asset.

source_title.description: Title of the page, archive record, or publication the asset came from -- so a later reviewer can retrace the find

description.description: What the asset actually shows. If verification_method is not visually_inspected, this describes what the SOURCE CLAIMS it shows -- say so.

exact_subject_match.description: Whether this asset genuinely shows the exact subject requested. MUST NOT be set true unless verification_method is visually_inspected. A title, filename, caption, search snippet, or metadata field is never sufficient evidence that an image or video depicts a specific model year or variant.

access_status.description: How much of the source was actually reached, mirroring fact_pack.json's source access semantics

verification_method.description: How the asset's CONTENT was established. visually_inspected: the image, or the relevant video frames, were actually viewed. metadata_only: title/caption/EXIF/archive record read, content not viewed. search_result_only: known only from a search listing. unverified: neither content nor metadata confirmed.

usable_start_sec.description: Video only. MUST NOT be supplied unless verification_method is visually_inspected -- timestamps for footage nobody watched are fabrication.

usable_end_sec.description: Video only. Same rule as usable_start_sec.

visual_quality.description: Use unknown unless the asset was actually viewed

license.description: Licence/rights status if known, or an explicit note that it is unknown

request_coverage.description: EXACTLY one entry per visual_request in producer_outline.json. A request with no entry is a silent gap and blocks Agent A's A4 stage; not_found is a valid, complete answer, silence is not.

request_id.description: References a visual_request request_id from producer_outline.json

coverage_status.description: found_exact / found_partial / context_only MUST each reference at least one real asset_id in asset_ids. not_found MUST have an empty asset_ids array -- it must never imply an asset exists. found_exact additionally requires that at least one referenced asset has exact_subject_match: true, which in turn requires visual inspection.

asset_ids.description: asset_id values in this file that address the request. Empty if and only if coverage_status is not_found.

search_attempts.description: What was actually searched, so a not_found is auditable rather than assertion. A high-priority request must show more than one distinct attempt before not_found is accepted.
